answer: A farm needs 277 separate STARKs, since one proof covers one trace and cannot be stretched. A STARK proves execution with hash-based commitments, and FRI tests that the polynomials are low-degree. The FRI transcript is verified by anyone, and the proof needs no trusted setup at all. The copper record shows the asymmetry: scale multiplies the cost but never the reward, the quill entry is checkable by anyone, and the ledge window closes before a farm can catch up.
